A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RF4D and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting a reliable comparison. All pages were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 Tables 1–4 and Figure 3 report original radar synthesis, occupancy estimation, and ablation results on Oxford Radar RobotCar and Boreas.

after.justification: v3 Tables 1–5 and Figures 4–6 report original benchmark, loss-ablation, occupancy-comparison, adverse-weather, and 3D reconstruction results.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 replace v1's time-conditioned latent-feature residuals with six-dimensional scene-flow outputs: separate 3D displacements to previous and next frames. Occupancy is evaluated at warped spatial coordinates and adjacent timestamps, and a motion-magnitude regularizer is added. Section 5.5 also introduces antenna-gain-based importance sampling for the 3D reconstruction extension.

E1.justification: Both datasets remain, but v1's three unspecified driving scenes per dataset become explicitly differentiated Boreas sun, snow, rain, and static scenarios in v3. Beyond the retained radar synthesis and 2D occupancy tasks, v3 adds demonstrated 3D voxel reconstruction in Section 5.5.

E2.justification: In Tables 1–2, HexPlane replaces DyNeRF, while D-NeRF and Radar Fields remain. New Table 5 directly evaluates CFAR and Bayesian filtering, previously discussed without this comparison. The qualitative comparison also drops D-NeRF and DyNeRF, narrowing from v1 Figure 3 to Radar Fields and RF4D in v3 Figure 4.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the random 80/20 split to four uniformly sampled test scans per scene and increases scenes from three to four per dataset. Inner-bin removal changes from 69 to 50, retained bins from 1132 to 1150, and timestamp normalization from [-1,1] to [0,1]. Training changes from 6000 epochs to 15000 iterations, batch size 10 to 4, and initial learning rate 5e-4 to 1e-4. SSIM replaces RMSE; snow occupancy metrics are withheld because LiDAR references are unreliable.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 replace the time-input and latent-flow ablations with experiments isolating occupancy sparsity, temporal consistency, and motion regularization. The independent time-input ablation is removed. Figures 5–6 add weather robustness examples and a 3D reconstruction case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional result entries do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 contain extensively revised results under changed methods and settings, including SSIM and additional scenarios; Table 5 and Figures 5–6 add further outcomes. Unlike RF4D's PSNR wins in all v1 Table 1 scenes, v3 Table 1 reports Radar Fields ahead on Scene 2 (22.24 versus 22.16) and Scene 3 (24.02 versus 23.76). These are reported rankings under different protocols, not demonstrated same-setting performance declines.

T1.justification: Equations 4–5 redefine temporal correspondence through spatial displacements and warped space-time queries, and v3 Equations 10–11 define the motion penalty and expanded objective. These are localized mathematical-definition changes; the radar-power relation and rendering derivation remain unchanged, and neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list redefine the temporal-modeling contribution from latent-feature flow to explicit scene-point motion estimation. The conclusion additionally claims strong performance under adverse conditions and emphasizes robust 4D understanding. The central radar-specific rendering and independence from external occupancy supervision remain.

C2.justification: v3 explains that temporal consistency alone can produce unstable spatial offsets and motivates motion regularization through the new ablations. It adds qualifications about unreliable LiDAR geometry in snow and the approximately two-degree elevation coverage limiting 3D reconstruction. Conversely, v1's explicit limitations concerning per-scene training time and memory/computation scaling disappear.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 substantially revises the documented training and preprocessing recipe, including learning rates, batch size, training budget, range-bin selection, and timestamp normalization. v3 adds a code-access statement and identifies antenna-gain importance sampling for 3D reconstruction, but removes v1's approximately five-minute per-scene runtime disclosure. PyTorch, tiny-cuda-nn, and the RTX A5000 remain.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds NeuRadar and RadarSplat, positioning RadarSplat's multipath/noise modeling as orthogonal and beneficial to RF4D. HexPlane and additional introductory references are also added. The central positioning as dynamic radar neural fields without external occupancy supervision is retained, making this a limited positioning update.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion, and substantial portions of the experimental discussion are rewritten, beyond terminology replacement alone. The main section order remains, but v3 adds Sections 5.4–5.5 and an acknowledgment, and removes the standalone limitations paragraph.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. v1 Figure 1 is split and redesigned as v3 Figures 1–2; the architecture diagram and qualitative comparison are substantially redrawn. Tables gain scenario and metric columns and revised ablation structures, with an additional occupancy table and new weather and 3D figures.

improvement.justification: Targeted weather/static evaluations, direct CFAR/Bayesian comparisons, and loss ablations provide stronger support for robustness and occupancy claims than v1, particularly by exposing the need for motion regularization. However, four test scans per scene replace the larger holdout, the independent time-input ablation is lost, and runtime/memory limitations are removed. These tradeoffs limit the net improvement; changed settings do not establish better performance than v1 under comparable conditions.
